subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` be an enforced per-DM tool policy, or should this accepted config surface be retired and diagnosed?
rationale: Current source accepts a security-sensitive direct DM policy shape but the runtime resolver remains group-scoped, so implementation direction changes a config/security contract rather than only filling in missing code.

options.title: Enforce Direct Policy
options.body: Keep the accepted schema and add a direct-aware resolver path that applies exact and wildcard DM tool policies with regression and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Retire Direct Policy Surface
options.body: Remove or reject `direct.*.tools`, add doctor/docs guidance, and tell users to use global or per-agent `toolsBySender` for sender-scoped tool control.

options.title: Defer To Broader Binding Policy
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on the broader per-binding policy discussion, but leave the accepted Telegram direct surface clearly warned or disabled in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct Policy
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted schema and add a direct-aware resolver path that applies exact and wildcard DM tool policies with regression and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest relevant main history points to steipete on trusted group facts and scoped group tool-policy resolution, which are central to choosing the safe resolver shape.
